subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart message-recovery design should be canonical for this issue: the current SQLite followup queue PR, an older narrower PR, or a broader restart recovery design?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the permanent fix touches persisted runtime state, message delivery semantics, and overlapping open PRs, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Advance SQLite queue PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 as the canonical candidate, resolve its proof and merge-risk issues, then close older overlapping PRs after the decision.

options.title: Narrow to drain mitigation
options.body: Choose a smaller drain-only approach such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 and leave durable replay for a separate explicit design.

options.title: Pause for broader recovery design
options.body: Keep the issue open under a wider gateway restart/session recovery plan before accepting new runtime storage or plugin API surface.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite queue PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 as the canonical candidate, resolve its proof and merge-risk issues, then close older overlapping PRs after the decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged restart-drain work makes this the clearest owner signal for choosing the gateway lifecycle boundary.
